# gh-1441: Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)

## Description

## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).

# PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom): ci.yml has
  # NO pull_request trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM
  # workflow_dispatch on the head SHA (machine-sm.yml), where the paths
  # classifier cannot run (no pull_request event diff). The leg is
  # therefore path-BLIND on dispatches: it runs in EVERY SM validation
  # (one hosted-macOS leg beside the build-macos/build-ios legs already
  # paid there), and the exzone path set only narrows a future real
  # pull_request trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the
  # nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them

# gh-1441: Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)

## Description

## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).
- The renderer node: `'voxel' => _voxel(m)` → `if (voxelWorld == null) return _mediaPlaceholder(m, Icons.landscape, label: 'Voxel world');` else `JsVoxelNode(world: voxelWorld!, …)` (`lib/src/renderer/json_widget_renderer.dart:619-623`). The constructor param doc states the contract: *"Engines expose their bridge-owned world; hosts rendering trees without an engine pass the world they fill."*

Fa app (this repo) — **both** `JsonWidgetRenderer` construction sites omit `voxelWorld`:

- fullscreen: `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`, `_treeView` (~:833) — passes `theme` / `mapTileProvider` / `mediaHost` / `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- live tile: `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart` (~:376) — `mediaHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- the Fa wrapper `JsAppEngine` keeps the runtime engine private (`JsWidgetEngine? _engine`, `js_app_engine.dart:307`; only `exportedState` / `peekLogs` are exposed) — there is no `voxelWorld` accessor either.

**Fix sketch:** add `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` to Fa's `JsAppEngine`, and pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at both renderer sites, mirroring the existing `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` wiring comments ("the SAME host the engine's JsRuntimeConfig got — see JsAppEngine.start").

## Evidence / reproduction

- Device: Fa iOS app (JavaScriptCore backend), 2026-10-09.
- **fa-craft 0.2.18** (catalog auto-update; `minRuntime 0.4.79`): screen = full-bleed "Voxel world" placeholder under the HUD crosshair. App log (repeated, stable):
  `{id: [facraft] v=0.2.18 fps=120 hud=0.4ms mesh=7.8ms uploads=25 meshKB=2021 native=true}` — the probe resolved, ~2 MB of chunk uploads accepted, per-frame `voxel.camera` flowing; nothing renders.
- **voxel-sandbox 1.0.0** (`minRuntime 0.4.127`): sky-blue 240 px box containing the same placeholder; the status row literally reads **"9 chunks · 1296 faces" / "voxel node live"** — the widget's own support probe resolved, so the banner claims the node is live while the pixels say otherwise.
- No JS errors in `app.log` (`widget eval error` absent); the trees contain a valid `{type:'voxel', id}` node, so the placeholder is the renderer's null-world fallback, not a parse failure.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — For an engine whose tree contains `{type:'voxel'}` after a successful `voxel.attach` + `voxel.mesh`, the fullscreen surface builds a `JsVoxelNode` and NOT the "Voxel world" `_mediaPlaceholder` (hook: widget test rendering the engine tree through the `js_app_view` body, `find.byType(JsVoxelNode)` / golden without the landscape icon).
- **AC2** — The same assertion holds for the live-tile surface (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`) when a tile tree contains a voxel node (hook: the existing tile test harness).
- **AC3** — Degradation contract intact: on a minimal custom backend where `backend.voxelWorld == null`, the placeholder still renders (no crash) AND a one-line diagnostic is logged so authoring agents can tell "host did not wire voxelWorld" from "broken widget" (hook: fake-backend test asserting the log record).
- **AC4** — The catalog fixtures `fa-craft` and `voxel-sandbox` render actual terrain in this repo's E2E/golden harness (hook: golden snapshots; both apps already exercise probe → upload → camera).
- **AC5** — Reload re-wires the CURRENT world: after `JsAppEngine.reload`/restart, a subsequent render uses the new engine's `voxelWorld` — never a stale world from the disposed engine (hook: test asserting instance identity across reload).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC5): `JsAppEngine.voxelWorld` returns `_engine.voxelWorld`; `null` before start and after dispose — pure fake backend.
- `IT-1` (AC1, AC3): `js_app_view` widget test with `MemoryExecutionEnv` + fixture widget (probe + one chunk + camera) asserting `JsVoxelNode` presence; null-world fake asserts placeholder + diagnostic log (fakes, deterministic clock).
- `IT-2` (AC2): the same fixture through the tile builder.
- `E2E-1` (AC4): golden render of the voxel-sandbox fixture at engine start and after a `dig` event; parity with the runtime's `test/voxel_sandbox_logic_test.dart` expectations (semantic-drift property: the two repos' goldens must not diverge silently).
- `REG-1` (AC1/AC2): a source pin-guard in the style of `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` — scan `js_app_view.dart` and `dynamic_widget_tile.dart`, assert every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` construction passes `voxelWorld:`. CI rule: **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` (backend parity): for every shipped backend (flutter_js/JSC, web worker) assert `engine.voxelWorld != null` after start, so the wiring cannot silently regress on one platform (negative control: the minimal test backend stays null by design — covered by IT-1's fake).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Voxel node in the FIRST tree, before any `voxel.*` call: the bridge world is eager (`js_widget_bridge.dart:134`), so with wiring the first frame already renders (empty sky) — test asserts no placeholder on a bare `{type:'voxel'}` tree with zero chunks.
- **E2** — Older runtime / rejecting hostCall: the widget's own probe rejects → apps keep their documented graceful paths (voxel-sandbox "voxel node unsupported" banner; fa-craft legacy `scene3d` fallback). Unchanged by this fix — pinned by a fake-backend rejection test.
- **E3** — Two engines live at once (fullscreen + tile of the same app): each renderer must get ITS engine's world; no cross-talk (test: two engines, distinct chunk colors).
- **E4** — Dispose/reload mid-flight: a pending `voxel.mesh` for a disposed engine must not paint into the new world (identity assert in UT-1/AC5).
- **E5** — `jsr.capture` (runtime 0.4.128+) on a voxel tree captures the rendered world, not the placeholder (golden hash differs from the placeholder golden).

## Non-goals

- No GPU/3D-engine rewrite of the voxel pipeline — upstream's "GPU vox…

- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).
- The renderer node: `'voxel' => _voxel(m)` → `if (voxelWorld == null) return _mediaPlaceholder(m, Icons.landscape, label: 'Voxel world');` else `JsVoxelNode(world: voxelWorld!, …)` (`lib/src/renderer/json_widget_renderer.dart:619-623`). The constructor param doc states the contract: *"Engines expose their bridge-owned world; hosts rendering trees without an engine pass the world they fill."*

Fa app (this repo) — **both** `JsonWidgetRenderer` construction sites omit `voxelWorld`:

- fullscreen: `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`, `_treeView` (~:833) — passes `theme` / `mapTileProvider` / `mediaHost` / `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- live tile: `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart` (~:376) — `mediaHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- the Fa wrapper `JsAppEngine` keeps the runtime engine private (`JsWidgetEngine? _engine`, `js_app_engine.dart:307`; only `exportedState` / `peekLogs` are exposed) — there is no `voxelWorld` accessor either.

**Fix sketch:** add `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` to Fa's `JsAppEngine`, and pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at both renderer sites, mirroring the existing `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` wiring comments ("the SAME host the engine's JsRuntimeConfig got — see JsAppEngine.start").

## Evidence / reproduction

- Device: Fa iOS app (JavaScriptCore backend), 2026-10-09.
- **fa-craft 0.2.18** (catalog auto-update; `minRuntime 0.4.79`): screen = full-bleed "Voxel world" placeholder under the HUD crosshair. App log (repeated, stable):
  `{id: [facraft] v=0.2.18 fps=120 hud=0.4ms mesh=7.8ms uploads=25 meshKB=2021 native=true}` — the probe resolved, ~2 MB of chunk uploads accepted, per-frame `voxel.camera` flowing; nothing renders.
- **voxel-sandbox 1.0.0** (`minRuntime 0.4.127`): sky-blue 240 px box containing the same placeholder; the status row literally reads **"9 chunks · 1296 faces" / "voxel node live"** — the widget's own support probe resolved, so the banner claims the node is live while the pixels say otherwise.
- No JS errors in `app.log` (`widget eval error` absent); the trees contain a valid `{type:'voxel', id}` node, so the placeholder is the renderer's null-world fallback, not a parse failure.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — For an engine whose tree contains `{type:'voxel'}` after a successful `voxel.attach` + `voxel.mesh`, the fullscreen surface builds a `JsVoxelNode` and NOT the "Voxel world" `_mediaPlaceholder` (hook: widget test rendering the engine tree through the `js_app_view` body, `find.byType(JsVoxelNode)` / golden without the landscape icon).
- **AC2** — The same assertion holds for the live-tile surface (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`) when a tile tree contains a voxel node (hook: the existing tile test harness).
- **AC3** — Degradation contract intact: on a minimal custom backend where `backend.voxelWorld == null`, the placeholder still renders (no crash) AND a one-line diagnostic is logged so authoring agents can tell "host did not wire voxelWorld" from "broken widget" (hook: fake-backend test asserting the log record).
- **AC4** — The catalog fixtures `fa-craft` and `voxel-sandbox` render actual terrain in this repo's E2E/golden harness (hook: golden snapshots; both apps already exercise probe → upload → camera).
- **AC5** — Reload re-wires the CURRENT world: after `JsAppEngine.reload`/restart, a subsequent render uses the new engine's `voxelWorld` — never a stale world from the disposed engine (hook: test asserting instance identity across reload).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC5): `JsAppEngine.voxelWorld` returns `_engine.voxelWorld`; `null` before start and after dispose — pure fake backend.
- `IT-1` (AC1, AC3): `js_app_view` widget test with `MemoryExecutionEnv` + fixture widget (probe + one chunk + camera) asserting `JsVoxelNode` presence; null-world fake asserts placeholder + diagnostic log (fakes, deterministic clock).
- `IT-2` (AC2): the same fixture through the tile builder.
- `E2E-1` (AC4): golden render of the voxel-sandbox fixture at engine start and after a `dig` event; parity with the runtime's `test/voxel_sandbox_logic_test.dart` expectations (semantic-drift property: the two repos' goldens must not diverge silently).
- `REG-1` (AC1/AC2): a source pin-guard in the style of `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` — scan `js_app_view.dart` and `dynamic_widget_tile.dart`, assert every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` construction passes `voxelWorld:`. CI rule: **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` (backend parity): for every shipped backend (flutter_js/JSC, web worker) assert `engine.voxelWorld != null` after start, so the wiring cannot silently regress on one platform (negative control: the minimal test backend stays null by design — covered by IT-1's fake).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Voxel node in the FIRST tree, before any `voxel.*` call: the bridge world is eager (`js_widget_bridge.dart:134`), so with wiring the first frame already renders (empty sky) — test asserts no placeholder on a bare `{type:'voxel'}` tree with zero chunks.
- **E2** — Older runtime / rejecting hostCall: the widget's own probe rejects → apps keep their documented graceful paths (voxel-sandbox "voxel node unsupported" banner; fa-craft legacy `scene3d` fallback). Unchanged by this fix — pinned by a fake-backend rejection test.
- **E3** — Two engines live at once (fullscreen + tile of the same app): each renderer must get ITS engine's world; no cross-talk (test: two engines, distinct chunk colors).
- **E4** — Dispose/reload mid-flight: a pending `voxel.mesh` for a disposed engine must not paint into the new world (identity assert in UT-1/AC5).
- **E5** — `jsr.capture` (runtime 0.4.128+) on a voxel tree captures the rendered world, not the placeholder …

# PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom): ci.yml has
  # NO pull_request trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM
  # workflow_dispatch on the head SHA (machine-sm.yml), where the paths
  # classifier cannot run (no pull_request event diff). The leg is
  # therefore path-BLIND on dispatches: it runs in EVERY SM validation
  # (one hosted-macOS leg beside the build-macos/build-ios legs already
  # paid there), and the exzone path set only narrows a future real
  # pull_request trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the
  # nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them

# gh-1441: Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)

## Description

## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).
- The renderer node: `'voxel' => _voxel(m)` → `if (voxelWorld == null) return _mediaPlaceholder(m, Icons.landscape, label: 'Voxel world');` else `JsVoxelNode(world: voxelWorld!, …)` (`lib/src/renderer/json_widget_renderer.dart:619-623`). The constructor param doc states the contract: *"Engines expose their bridge-owned world; hosts rendering trees without an engine pass the world they fill."*

Fa app (this repo) — **both** `JsonWidgetRenderer` construction sites omit `voxelWorld`:

- fullscreen: `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`, `_treeView` (~:833) — passes `theme` / `mapTileProvider` / `mediaHost` / `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- live tile: `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart` (~:376) — `mediaHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- the Fa wrapper `JsAppEngine` keeps the runtime engine private (`JsWidgetEngine? _engine`, `js_app_engine.dart:307`; only `exportedState` / `peekLogs` are exposed) — there is no `voxelWorld` accessor either.

**Fix sketch:** add `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` to Fa's `JsAppEngine`, and pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at both renderer sites, mirroring the existing `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` wiring comments ("the SAME host the engine's JsRuntimeConfig got — see JsAppEngine.start").

## Evidence / reproduction

- Device: Fa iOS app (JavaScriptCore backend), 2026-10-09.
- **fa-craft 0.2.18** (catalog auto-update; `minRuntime 0.4.79`): screen = full-bleed "Voxel world" placeholder under the HUD crosshair. App log (repeated, stable):
  `{id: [facraft] v=0.2.18 fps=120 hud=0.4ms mesh=7.8ms uploads=25 meshKB=2021 native=true}` — the probe resolved, ~2 MB of chunk uploads accepted, per-frame `voxel.camera` flowing; nothing renders.
- **voxel-sandbox 1.0.0** (`minRuntime 0.4.127`): sky-blue 240 px box containing the same placeholder; the status row literally reads **"9 chunks · 1296 faces" / "voxel node live"** — the widget's own support probe resolved, so the banner claims the node is live while the pixels say otherwise.
- No JS errors in `app.log` (`widget eval error` absent); the trees contain a valid `{type:'voxel', id}` node, so the placeholder is the renderer's null-world fallback, not a parse failure.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — For an engine whose tree contains `{type:'voxel'}` after a successful `voxel.attach` + `voxel.mesh`, the fullscreen surface builds a `JsVoxelNode` and NOT the "Voxel world" `_mediaPlaceholder` (hook: widget test rendering the engine tree through the `js_app_view` body, `find.byType(JsVoxelNode)` / golden without the landscape icon).
- **AC2** — The same assertion holds for the live-tile surface (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`) when a tile tree contains a voxel node (hook: the existing tile test harness).
- **AC3** — Degradation contract intact: on a minimal custom backend where `backend.voxelWorld == null`, the placeholder still renders (no crash) AND a one-line diagnostic is logged so authoring agents can tell "host did not wire voxelWorld" from "broken widget" (hook: fake-backend test asserting the log record).
- **AC4** — The catalog fixtures `fa-craft` and `voxel-sandbox` render actual terrain in this repo's E2E/golden harness (hook: golden snapshots; both apps already exercise probe → upload → camera).
- **AC5** — Reload re-wires the CURRENT world: after `JsAppEngine.reload`/restart, a subsequent render uses the new engine's `voxelWorld` — never a stale world from the disposed engine (hook: test asserting instance identity across reload).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC5): `JsAppEngine.voxelWorld` returns `_engine.voxelWorld`; `null` before start and after dispose — pure fake backend.
- `IT-1` (AC1, AC3): `js_app_view` widget test with `MemoryExecutionEnv` + fixture widget (probe + one chunk + camera) asserting `JsVoxelNode` presence; null-world fake asserts placeholder + diagnostic log (fakes, deterministic clock).
- `IT-2` (AC2): the same fixture through the tile builder.
- `E2E-1` (AC4): golden render of the voxel-sandbox fixture at engine start and after a `dig` event; parity with the runtime's `test/voxel_sandbox_logic_test.dart` expectations (semantic-drift property: the two repos' goldens must not diverge silently).
- `REG-1` (AC1/AC2): a source pin-guard in the style of `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` — scan `js_app_view.dart` and `dynamic_widget_tile.dart`, assert every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` construction passes `voxelWorld:`. CI rule: **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` (backend parity): for every shipped backend (flutter_js/JSC, web worker) assert `engine.voxelWorld != null` after start, so the wiring cannot silently regress on one platform (negative control: the minimal test backend stays null by design — covered by IT-1's fake).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Voxel node in the FIRST tree, before any `voxel.*` call: the bridge world is eager (`js_widget_bridge.dart:134`), so with wiring the first frame already renders (empty sky) — test asserts no placeholder on a bare `{type:'voxel'}` tree with zero chunks.
- **E2** — Older runtime / rejecting hostCall: the widget's own probe rejects → apps keep their documented graceful paths (voxel-sandbox "voxel node unsupported" banner; fa-craft legacy `scene3d` fallback). Unchanged by this fix — pinned by a fake-backend rejection test.
- **E3** — Two engines live at once (fullscreen + tile of the same app): each renderer must get ITS engine's world; no cross-talk (test: two engines, distinct chunk colors).
- **E4** — Dispose/reload mid-flight: a pending `voxel.mesh` for a disposed engine must not paint into the new world (identity assert in UT-1/AC5).
- **E5** — `jsr.capture` (runtime 0.4.128+) on a voxel tree captures the rendered world, not the placeholder (golden hash differs from the placeholder golden).

## Non-goals

- No GPU/3D-engine rewrite of the voxel pipeline — upstream's "GPU vox…

# PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom): ci.yml has
  # NO pull_request trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM
  # workflow_dispatch on the head SHA (machine-sm.yml), where the paths
  # classifier cannot run (no pull_request event diff). The leg is
  # therefore path-BLIND on dispatches: it runs in EVERY SM validation
  # (one hosted-macOS leg beside the build-macos/build-ios legs already
  # paid there), and the exzone path set only narrows a future real
  # pull_request trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the
  # nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2

# gh-1441: Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)

## Description

## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).
- The renderer node: `'voxel' => _voxel(m)` → `if (voxelWorld == null) return _mediaPlaceholder(m, Icons.landscape, label: 'Voxel world');` else `JsVoxelNode(world: voxelWorld!, …)` (`lib/src/renderer/json_widget_renderer.dart:619-623`). The constructor param doc states the contract: *"Engines expose their bridge-owned world; hosts rendering trees without an engine pass the world they fill."*

Fa app (this repo) — **both** `JsonWidgetRenderer` construction sites omit `voxelWorld`:

- fullscreen: `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`, `_treeView` (~:833) — passes `theme` / `mapTileProvider` / `mediaHost` / `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- live tile: `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart` (~:376) — `mediaHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- the Fa wrapper `JsAppEngine` keeps the runtime engine private (`JsWidgetEngine? _engine`, `js_app_engine.dart:307`; only `exportedState` / `peekLogs` are exposed) — there is no `voxelWorld` accessor either.

**Fix sketch:** add `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` to Fa's `JsAppEngine`, and pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at both renderer sites, mirroring the existing `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` wiring comments ("the SAME host the engine's JsRuntimeConfig got — see JsAppEngine.start").

## Evidence / reproduction

- Device: Fa iOS app (JavaScriptCore backend), 2026-10-09.
- **fa-craft 0.2.18** (catalog auto-update; `minRuntime 0.4.79`): screen = full-bleed "Voxel world" placeholder under the HUD crosshair. App log (repeated, stable):
  `{id: [facraft] v=0.2.18 fps=120 hud=0.4ms mesh=7.8ms uploads=25 meshKB=2021 native=true}` — the probe resolved, ~2 MB of chunk uploads accepted, per-frame `voxel.camera` flowing; nothing renders.
- **voxel-sandbox 1.0.0** (`minRuntime 0.4.127`): sky-blue 240 px box containing the same placeholder; the status row literally reads **"9 chunks · 1296 faces" / "voxel node live"** — the widget's own support probe resolved, so the banner claims the node is live while the pixels say otherwise.
- No JS errors in `app.log` (`widget eval error` absent); the trees contain a valid `{type:'voxel', id}` node, so the placeholder is the renderer's null-world fallback, not a parse failure.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — For an engine whose tree contains `{type:'voxel'}` after a successful `voxel.attach` + `voxel.mesh`, the fullscreen surface builds a `JsVoxelNode` and NOT the "Voxel world" `_mediaPlaceholder` (hook: widget test rendering the engine tree through the `js_app_view` body, `find.byType(JsVoxelNode)` / golden without the landscape icon).
- **AC2** — The same assertion holds for the live-tile surface (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`) when a tile tree contains a voxel node (hook: the existing tile test harness).
- **AC3** — Degradation contract intact: on a minimal custom backend where `backend.voxelWorld == null`, the placeholder still renders (no crash) AND a one-line diagnostic is logged so authoring agents can tell "host did not wire voxelWorld" from "broken widget" (hook: fake-backend test asserting the log record).
- **AC4** — The catalog fixtures `fa-craft` and `voxel-sandbox` render actual terrain in this repo's E2E/golden harness (hook: golden snapshots; both apps already exercise probe → upload → camera).
- **AC5** — Reload re-wires the CURRENT world: after `JsAppEngine.reload`/restart, a subsequent render uses the new engine's `voxelWorld` — never a stale world from the disposed engine (hook: test asserting instance identity across reload).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC5): `JsAppEngine.voxelWorld` returns `_engine.voxelWorld`; `null` before start and after dispose — pure fake backend.
- `IT-1` (AC1, AC3): `js_app_view` widget test with `MemoryExecutionEnv` + fixture widget (probe + one chunk + camera) asserting `JsVoxelNode` presence; null-world fake asserts placeholder + diagnostic log (fakes, deterministic clock).
- `IT-2` (AC2): the same fixture through the tile builder.
- `E2E-1` (AC4): golden render of the voxel-sandbox fixture at engine start and after a `dig` event; parity with the runtime's `test/voxel_sandbox_logic_test.dart` expectations (semantic-drift property: the two repos' goldens must not diverge silently).
- `REG-1` (AC1/AC2): a source pin-guard in the style of `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` — scan `js_app_view.dart` and `dynamic_widget_tile.dart`, assert every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` construction passes `voxelWorld:`. CI rule: **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` (backend parity): for every shipped backend (flutter_js/JSC, web worker) assert `engine.voxelWorld != null` after start, so the wiring cannot silently regress on one platform (negative control: the minimal test backend stays null by design — covered by IT-1's fake).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Voxel node in the FIRST tree, before any `voxel.*` call: the bridge world is eager (`js_widget_bridge.dart:134`), so with wiring the first frame already renders (empty sky) — test asserts no placeholder on a bare `{type:'voxel'}` tree with zero chunks.
- **E2** — Older runtime / rejecting hostCall: the widget's own probe rejects → apps keep their documented graceful paths (voxel-sandbox "voxel node unsupported" banner; fa-craft legacy `scene3d` fallback). Unchanged by this fix — pinned by a fake-backend rejection test.
- **E3** — Two engines live at once (fullscreen + tile of the same app): each renderer must get ITS engine's world; no cross-talk (test: two engines, distinct chunk colors).
- **E4** — Dispose/reload mid-flight: a pending `voxel.mesh` for a disposed engine must not paint into the new world (identity assert in UT-1/AC5).
- **E5** — `jsr.capture` (runtime 0.4.128+) on a voxel tree captures the rendered world, not the placeholder (golden hash differs from the placeholder golden).

## Non-goals

- No GPU/3D-engine rewrite of the voxel pipeline — upstream's "GPU vox…

# gh-1441: Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)

## Description

## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).
- The renderer node: `'voxel' => _voxel(m)` → `if (voxelWorld == null) return _mediaPlaceholder(m, Icons.landscape, label: 'Voxel world');` else `JsVoxelNode(world: voxelWorld!, …)` (`lib/src/renderer/json_widget_renderer.dart:619-623`). The constructor param doc states the contract: *"Engines expose their bridge-owned world; hosts rendering trees without an engine pass the world they fill."*

Fa app (this repo) — **both** `JsonWidgetRenderer` construction sites omit `voxelWorld`:

- fullscreen: `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`, `_treeView` (~:833) — passes `theme` / `mapTileProvider` / `mediaHost` / `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- live tile: `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart` (~:376) — `mediaHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- the Fa wrapper `JsAppEngine` keeps the runtime engine private (`JsWidgetEngine? _engine`, `js_app_engine.dart:307`; only `exportedState` / `peekLogs` are exposed) — there is no `voxelWorld` accessor either.

**Fix sketch:** add `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` to Fa's `JsAppEngine`, and pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at both renderer sites, mirroring the existing `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` wiring comments ("the SAME host the engine's JsRuntimeConfig got — see JsAppEngine.start").

## Evidence / reproduction

- Device: Fa iOS app (JavaScriptCore backend), 2026-10-09.
- **fa-craft 0.2.18** (catalog auto-update; `minRuntime 0.4.79`): screen = full-bleed "Voxel world" placeholder under the HUD crosshair. App log (repeated, stable):
  `{id: [facraft] v=0.2.18 fps=120 hud=0.4ms mesh=7.8ms uploads=25 meshKB=2021 native=true}` — the probe resolved, ~2 MB of chunk uploads accepted, per-frame `voxel.camera` flowing; nothing renders.
- **voxel-sandbox 1.0.0** (`minRuntime 0.4.127`): sky-blue 240 px box containing the same placeholder; the status row literally reads **"9 chunks · 1296 faces" / "voxel node live"** — the widget's own support probe resolved, so the banner claims the node is live while the pixels say otherwise.
- No JS errors in `app.log` (`widget eval error` absent); the trees contain a valid `{type:'voxel', id}` node, so the placeholder is the renderer's null-world fallback, not a parse failure.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — For an engine whose tree contains `{type:'voxel'}` after a successful `voxel.attach` + `voxel.mesh`, the fullscreen surface builds a `JsVoxelNode` and NOT the "Voxel world" `_mediaPlaceholder` (hook: widget test rendering the engine tree through the `js_app_view` body, `find.byType(JsVoxelNode)` / golden without the landscape icon).
- **AC2** — The same assertion holds for the live-tile surface (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`) when a tile tree contains a voxel node (hook: the existing tile test harness).
- **AC3** — Degradation contract intact: on a minimal custom backend where `backend.voxelWorld == null`, the placeholder still renders (no crash) AND a one-line diagnostic is logged so authoring agents can tell "host did not wire voxelWorld" from "broken widget" (hook: fake-backend test asserting the log record).
- **AC4** — The catalog fixtures `fa-craft` and `voxel-sandbox` render actual terrain in this repo's E2E/golden harness (hook: golden snapshots; both apps already exercise probe → upload → camera).
- **AC5** — Reload re-wires the CURRENT world: after `JsAppEngine.reload`/restart, a subsequent render uses the new engine's `voxelWorld` — never a stale world from the disposed engine (hook: test asserting instance identity across reload).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC5): `JsAppEngine.voxelWorld` returns `_engine.voxelWorld`; `null` before start and after dispose — pure fake backend.
- `IT-1` (AC1, AC3): `js_app_view` widget test with `MemoryExecutionEnv` + fixture widget (probe + one chunk + camera) asserting `JsVoxelNode` presence; null-world fake asserts placeholder + diagnostic log (fakes, deterministic clock).
- `IT-2` (AC2): the same fixture through the tile builder.
- `E2E-1` (AC4): golden render of the voxel-sandbox fixture at engine start and after a `dig` event; parity with the runtime's `test/voxel_sandbox_logic_test.dart` expectations (semantic-drift property: the two repos' goldens must not diverge silently).
- `REG-1` (AC1/AC2): a source pin-guard in the style of `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` — scan `js_app_view.dart` and `dynamic_widget_tile.dart`, assert every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` construction passes `voxelWorld:`. CI rule: **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` (backend parity): for every shipped backend (flutter_js/JSC, web worker) assert `engine.voxelWorld != null` after start, so the wiring cannot silently regress on one platform (negative control: the minimal test backend stays null by design — covered by IT-1's fake).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Voxel node in the FIRST tree, before any `voxel.*` call: the bridge world is eager (`js_widget_bridge.dart:134`), so with wiring the first frame already renders (empty sky) — test asserts no placeholder on a bare `{type:'voxel'}` tree with zero chunks.
- **E2** — Older runtime / rejecting hostCall: the widget's own probe rejects → apps keep their documented graceful paths (voxel-sandbox "voxel node unsupported" banner; fa-craft legacy `scene3d` fallback). Unchanged by this fix — pinned by a fake-backend rejection test.
- **E3** — Two engines live at once (fullscreen + tile of the same app): each renderer must get ITS engine's world; no cross-talk (test: two engines, distinct chunk colors).
- **E4** — Dispose/reload mid-flight: a pending `voxel.mesh` for a disposed engine must not paint into the new world (identity assert in UT-1/AC5).
- **E5** — `jsr.capture` (runtime 0.4.128+) on a voxel tree captures the rendered world, not the placeholder (golden hash differs from the placeholder golden).

## Non-goals

- No GPU/3D-engine rewrite of the voxel pipeline — upstream's "GPU vox…

- **fa-craft 0.2.18** (catalog auto-update; `minRuntime 0.4.79`): screen = full-bleed "Voxel world" placeholder under the HUD crosshair. App log (repeated, stable):
  `{id: [facraft] v=0.2.18 fps=120 hud=0.4ms mesh=7.8ms uploads=25 meshKB=2021 native=true}` — the probe resolved, ~2 MB of chunk uploads accepted, per-frame `voxel.camera` flowing; nothing renders.
- **voxel-sandbox 1.0.0** (`minRuntime 0.4.127`): sky-blue 240 px box containing the same placeholder; the status row literally reads **"9 chunks · 1296 faces" / "voxel node live"** — the widget's own support probe resolved, so the banner claims the node is live while the pixels say otherwise.
- No JS errors in `app.log` (`widget eval error` absent); the trees contain a valid `{type:'voxel', id}` node, so the placeholder is the renderer's null-world fallback, not a parse failure.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — For an engine whose tree contains `{type:'voxel'}` after a successful `voxel.attach` + `voxel.mesh`, the fullscreen surface builds a `JsVoxelNode` and NOT the "Voxel world" `_mediaPlaceholder` (hook: widget test rendering the engine tree through the `js_app_view` body, `find.byType(JsVoxelNode)` / golden without the landscape icon).
- **AC2** — The same assertion holds for the live-tile surface (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`) when a tile tree contains a voxel node (hook: the existing tile test harness).
- **AC3** — Degradation contract intact: on a minimal custom backend where `backend.voxelWorld == null`, the placeholder still renders (no crash) AND a one-line diagnostic is logged so authoring agents can tell "host did not wire voxelWorld" from "broken widget" (hook: fake-backend test asserting the log record).
- **AC4** — The catalog fixtures `fa-craft` and `voxel-sandbox` render actual terrain in this repo's E2E/golden harness (hook: golden snapshots; both apps already exercise probe → upload → camera).
- **AC5** — Reload re-wires the CURRENT world: after `JsAppEngine.reload`/restart, a subsequent render uses the new engine's `voxelWorld` — never a stale world from the disposed engine (hook: test asserting instance identity across reload).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC5): `JsAppEngine.voxelWorld` returns `_engine.voxelWorld`; `null` before start and after dispose — pure fake backend.
- `IT-1` (AC1, AC3): `js_app_view` widget test with `MemoryExecutionEnv` + fixture widget (probe + one chunk + camera) asserting `JsVoxelNode` presence; null-world fake asserts placeholder + diagnostic log (fakes, deterministic clock).
- `IT-2` (AC2): the same fixture through the tile builder.
- `E2E-1` (AC4): golden render of the voxel-sandbox fixture at engine start and after a `dig` event; parity with the runtime's `test/voxel_sandbox_logic_test.dart` expectations (semantic-drift property: the two repos' goldens must not diverge silently).
- `REG-1` (AC1/AC2): a source pin-guard in the style of `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` — scan `js_app_view.dart` and `dynamic_widget_tile.dart`, assert every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` construction passes `voxelWorld:`. CI rule: **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` (backend parity): for every shipped backend (flutter_js/JSC, web worker) assert `engine.voxelWorld != null` after start, so the wiring cannot silently regress on one platform (negative control: the minimal test backend stays null by design — covered by IT-1's fake).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Voxel node in the FIRST tree, before any `voxel.*` call: the bridge world is eager (`js_widget_bridge.dart:134`), so with wiring the first frame already renders (empty sky) — test asserts no placeholder on a bare `{type:'voxel'}` tree with zero chunks.
- **E2** — Older runtime / rejecting hostCall: the widget's own probe rejects → apps keep their documented graceful paths (voxel-sandbox "voxel node unsupported" banner; fa-craft legacy `scene3d` fallback). Unchanged by this fix — pinned by a fake-backend rejection test.
- **E3** — Two engines live at once (fullscreen + tile of the same app): each renderer must get ITS engine's world; no cross-talk (test: two engines, distinct chunk colors).
- **E4** — Dispose/reload mid-flight: a pending `voxel.mesh` for a disposed engine must not paint into the new world (identity assert in UT-1/AC5).
- **E5** — `jsr.capture` (runtime 0.4.128+) on a voxel tree captures the rendered world, not the placeholder …

# PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom): ci.yml has
  # NO pull_request trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM
  # workflow_dispatch on the head SHA (machine-sm.yml), where the paths
  # classifier cannot run (no pull_request event diff). The leg is
  # therefore path-BLIND on dispatches: it runs in EVERY SM validation
  # (one hosted-macOS leg beside the build-macos/build-ios legs already
  # paid there), and the exzone path set only narrows a future real
  # pull_request trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the
  # nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them

{
  "key": "gh-1441",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)",
    "description": "## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).
- The renderer node: `'voxel' => _voxel(m)` → `if (voxelWorld == null) return _mediaPlaceholder(m, Icons.landscape, label: 'Voxel world');` else `JsVoxelNode(world: voxelWorld!, …)` (`lib/src/renderer/json_widget_renderer.dart:619-623`). The constructor param doc states the contract: *"Engines expose their bridge-owned world; hosts rendering trees without an engine pass the world they fill."*

Fa app (this repo) — **both** `JsonWidgetRenderer` construction sites omit `voxelWorld`:

- fullscreen: `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`, `_treeView` (~:833) — passes `theme` / `mapTileProvider` / `mediaHost` / `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- live tile: `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart` (~:376) — `mediaHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- the Fa wrapper `JsAppEngine` keeps the runtime engine private (`JsWidgetEngine? _engine`, `js_app_engine.dart:307`; only `exportedState` / `peekLogs` are exposed) — there is no `voxelWorld` accessor either.

**Fix sketch:** add `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` to Fa's `JsAppEngine`, and pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at both renderer sites, mirroring the existing `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` wiring comments ("the SAME host the engine's JsRuntimeConfig got — see JsAppEngine.start").

## Evidence / reproduction

- Device: Fa iOS app (JavaScriptCore backend), 2026-10-09.
- **fa-craft 0.2.18** (catalog auto-update; `minRuntime 0.4.79`): screen = full-bleed "Voxel world" placeholder under the HUD crosshair. App log (repeated, stable):
  `{id: [facraft] v=0.2.18 fps=120 hud=0.4ms mesh=7.8ms uploads=25 meshKB=2021 native=true}` — the probe resolved, ~2 MB of chunk uploads accepted, per-frame `voxel.camera` flowing; nothing renders.
- **voxel-sandbox 1.0.0** (`minRuntime 0.4.127`): sky-blue 240 px box containing the same placeholder; the status row literally reads **"9 chunks · 1296 faces" / "voxel node live"** — the widget's own support probe resolved, so the banner claims the node is live while the pixels say otherwise.
- No JS errors in `app.log` (`widget eval error` absent); the trees contain a valid `{type:'voxel', id}` node, so the placeholder is the renderer's null-world fallback, not a parse failure.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — For an engine whose tree contains `{type:'voxel'}` after a successful `voxel.attach` + `voxel.mesh`, the fullscreen surface builds a `JsVoxelNode` and NOT the "Voxel world" `_mediaPlaceholder` (hook: widget test rendering the engine tree through the `js_app_view` body, `find.byType(JsVoxelNode)` / golden without the landscape icon).
- **AC2** — The same assertion holds for the live-tile surface (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`) when a tile tree contains a voxel node (hook: the existing tile test harness).
- **AC3** — Degradation contract intact: on a minimal custom backend where `backend.voxelWorld == null`, the placeholder still renders (no crash) AND a one-line diagnostic is logged so authoring agents can tell "host did not wire voxelWorld" from "broken widget" (hook: fake-backend test asserting the log record).
- **AC4** — The catalog fixtures `fa-craft` and `voxel-sandbox` render actual terrain in this repo's E2E/golden harness (hook: golden snapshots; both apps already exercise probe → upload → camera).
- **AC5** — Reload re-wires the CURRENT world: after `JsAppEngine.reload`/restart, a subsequent render uses the new engine's `voxelWorld` — never a stale world from the disposed engine (hook: test asserting instance identity across reload).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC5): `JsAppEngine.voxelWorld` returns `_engine.voxelWorld`; `null` before start and after dispose — pure fake backend.
- `IT-1` (AC1, AC3): `js_app_view` widget test with `MemoryExecutionEnv` + fixture widget (probe + one chunk + camera) asserting `JsVoxelNode` presence; null-world fake asserts placeholder + diagnostic log (fakes, deterministic clock).
- `IT-2` (AC2): the same fixture through the tile builder.
- `E2E-1` (AC4): golden render of the voxel-sandbox fixture at engine start and after a `dig` event; parity with the runtime's `test/voxel_sandbox_logic_test.dart` expectations (semantic-drift property: the two repos' goldens must not diverge silently).
- `REG-1` (AC1/AC2): a source pin-guard in the style of `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` — scan `js_app_view.dart` and `dynamic_widget_tile.dart`, assert every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` construction passes `voxelWorld:`. CI rule: **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` (backend parity): for every shipped backend (flutter_js/JSC, web worker) assert `engine.voxelWorld != null` after start, so the wiring cannot silently regress on one platform (negative control: the minimal test backend stays null by design — covered by IT-1's fake).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Voxel node in the FIRST tree, before any `voxel.*` call: the bridge world is eager (`js_widget_bridge.dart:134`), so with wiring the first frame already renders (empty sky) — test asserts no placeholder on a bare `{type:'voxel'}` tree with zero chunks.
- **E2** — Older runtime / rejecting hostCall: the widget's own probe rejects → apps keep their documented graceful paths (voxel-sandbox "voxel node unsupported" banner; fa-craft legacy `scene3d` fallback). Unchanged by this fix — pinned by a fake-backend rejection test.
- **E3** — Two engines live at once (fullscreen + tile of the same app): each renderer must get ITS engine's world; no cross-talk (test: two engines, distinct chunk colors).
- **E4** — Dispose/reload mid-flight: a pending `voxel.mesh` for a disposed engine must not paint into the new world (identity assert in UT-1/AC5).
- **E5** — `jsr.capture` (runtime 0.4.128+) on a voxel tree captures the rendered world, not the placeholder …

# PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom): ci.yml has
  # NO pull_request trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM
  # workflow_dispatch on the head SHA (machine-sm.yml), where the paths
  # classifier cannot run (no pull_request event diff). The leg is
  # therefore path-BLIND on dispatches: it runs in EVERY SM validation
  # (one hosted-macOS leg beside the build-macos/build-ios legs already
  # paid there), and the exzone path set only narrows a future real
  # pull_request trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the
  # nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

# PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom): ci.yml has
  # NO pull_request trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM
  # workflow_dispatch on the head SHA (machine-sm.yml), where the paths
  # classifier cannot run (no pull_request event diff). The leg is
  # therefore path-BLIND on dispatches: it runs in EVERY SM validation
  # (one hosted-macOS leg beside the build-macos/build-ios legs already
  # paid there), and the exzone path set only narrows a future real
  # pull_request trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the
  # nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them

# PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom): ci.yml has
  # NO pull_request trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM
  # workflow_dispatch on the head SHA (machine-sm.yml), where the paths
  # classifier cannot run (no pull_request event diff). The leg is
  # therefore path-BLIND on dispatches: it runs in EVERY SM validation
  # (one hosted-macOS leg beside the build-macos/build-ios legs already
  # paid there), and the exzone path set only narrows a future real
  # pull_request trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the
  # nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

# PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom): ci.yml has
  # NO pull_request trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM
  # workflow_dispatch on the head SHA (machine-sm.yml), where the paths
  # classifier cannot run (no pull_request event diff). The leg is
  # therefore path-BLIND on dispatches: it runs in EVERY SM validation
  # (one hosted-macOS leg beside the build-macos/build-ios legs already
  # paid there), and the exzone path set only narrows a future real
  # pull_request trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the
  # nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them

# PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom): ci.yml has
  # NO pull_request trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM
  # workflow_dispatch on the head SHA (machine-sm.yml), where the paths
  # classifier cannot run (no pull_request event diff). The leg is
  # therefore path-BLIND on dispatches: it runs in EVERY SM validation
  # (one hosted-macOS leg beside the build-macos/build-ios legs already
  # paid there), and the exzone path set only narrows a future real
  # pull_request trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the
  # nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

# PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 binaries-pr idiom): ci.yml has
  # NO pull_request trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM
  # workflow_dispatch on the head SHA (machine-sm.yml), where the paths
  # classifier cannot run (no pull_request event diff). The leg is
  # therefore path-BLIND on dispatches: it runs in EVERY SM validation
  # (one hosted-macOS leg beside the build-macos/build-ios legs already
  # paid there), and the exzone path set only narrows a future real
  # pull_request trigger. Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the
  # nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps
